description: Frozen M00 acceptance targets, not measurements, advertised limits, industry averages or evidence of enterprise readiness. This contract suite neither generates GiB reports nor runs a benchmark.

hardware.cpuModel: AMD EPYC 7313P, 16 assigned vCPUs on a dedicated reference host
hardware.storageMedia: Local enterprise NVMe SSD, no shared external contention
hardware.availability: Not provisioned or measured by M00. Future run manifests must record the actual CPU, allocation, disk/fs, database settings, kernel, topology and competing workloads.

measurementConditions.protocol: Record commit/toolchain, schema/parser revision, fixture digest and seed, exact per-process CPU/RSS/pool limits, network and database settings. Warm for 5 minutes, measure 30 minutes at declared concurrency, repeat 3 times. Report each run's p95/p99 and worst result, not only a cross-run average. Capture errors, rejections, queue age and observation reconciliation as well as throughput.
measurementConditions.scalingProtocol: Compare one then two equally budgeted parser processes with the same input distribution and fixed API/database/S3/reconciler resources. Demonstrate database, storage and CPU headroom first. Require interactive budgets concurrently; report saturation rather than increasing downstream resources mid-comparison.

fixtureGeneratorSpecification.identity: Derive stable synthetic workspace/asset/source/finding IDs from seed plus ordinal. Generate distinct scan IDs per cycle and distinct attempt IDs per redelivery. Repeat the same immutable payload for repeated imports; change only declared parser revisions during renormalization.
fixtureGeneratorSpecification.distribution: Deterministically assign records by ordinal modulo 1000 to the declared size buckets and workspace shares. Emit incrementally in fixed UTF-8 key order; pad with legal container whitespace to reach the exact report byte count without exceeding any record bound. Record exact generated digests, counts and invalid/oversize fixture labels.
fixtureGeneratorSpecification.formats: Synthetic JSON uses an object with data=synthetic and a records array. Synthetic XML uses a records root with synthetic record elements, no DTD, external entities or XInclude. They are streaming test grammars, not claims that every scanner adapter streams.

fixtureFormats.sizeDistribution: By record count: 950/1000 records at 1 KiB, 45/1000 at 16 KiB and 5/1000 at 1 MiB. Report mix by job count: 70% 10 MiB, 25% 100 MiB, 5% 1 GiB. Bounds include complete encoded records, not only message strings.
fixtureFormats.supportMeaning: The proposed synthetic grammar can be streamed. No production JSON parser or size support has been implemented.
fixtureFormats.rejectionPolicy: Bound depth, individual strings, total bytes, records and decompression ratio. Report rejected records explicitly; malformed or truncated reports cannot authorize source absence.

fixtureFormats.sizeDistribution: By record count: 980/1000 records at 2 KiB, 19/1000 at 64 KiB and 1/1000 at 4 MiB. Report mix by job count: 80% 10 MiB, 15% 100 MiB, 5% 1 GiB. XML records have their own bound; do not inherit JSON's.
fixtureFormats.supportMeaning: The proposed synthetic grammar can be streamed. No production XML parser or universal ZAP/report-size support is claimed.
fixtureFormats.rejectionPolicy: Reject external entity/DTD resolution and enforce depth, text-node, record and report limits. No external resource fetches are permitted.

budgets.measurement: Server-side duration of authorized list/detail requests during the declared mixed load, including database pool wait and response serialization, excluding client network time. Report each endpoint separately.
Same request population and per-endpoint breakdown as interactive-p95; do not hide timeout/error rates or failed requests from the report.

Maximum per-parser process RSS, including runtime and buffers, sampled through a supported 1 GiB synthetic JSON/XML import with its declared maximum record size. This is not a file-size or container-request measurement.
Durably emitted normalized input bytes per second for two versus one parser under the scaling protocol, only with verified downstream headroom and passing concurrent interactive budgets.

After controlled failure recovery/replay, compare durable acknowledged manifest membership to unique persisted observations. Pending/failed work must remain addressable and visibly incomplete until resolved.
Count duplicate domain mutations for the same intent/receipt after duplicate delivery and lost acknowledgment. Ambiguous external delivery stays uncertain rather than blindly retried.
Count source-resolution changes caused by failed, incomplete, delta, stale, mismatched-scope or locally failed inputs, and any ingestion override of a human decision.

Worst completed history-churn cycle's net logical data plus immutable object-store bytes after the declared retention/compaction checkpoint, excluding indexes counted separately. Also report gross written bytes and WAL; identical payload reuse must preserve scan membership.
Worst completed cycle's total PostgreSQL index growth after the same retention checkpoint. Report per-index size, dead tuples, vacuum debt and WAL bytes instead of hiding maintenance cost.

Elapsed restore of the history-churn subset's database, objects/manifests, config and required encryption material into fresh owned resources, ending only after digest/link, decisions and cross-service checks pass.
Count all transport/SDK/service attempts, including retries, against one logical request in deterministic throttling fixtures.
Wall-clock or controlled-clock duration from the first permitted attempt to final result or visible blocked/exhausted state, inclusive of Retry-After waits. Never retry past the overall deadline.

Maximum time from an eligible small-workspace batch becoming queued to its first durable stage progress during an 80%-dominant workspace burst. Record deliberately blocked jobs separately, with reasons.
Time from a controlled loss of stage progress to an actionable stalled-stage state observable by the authorized API/UI, while HTTP liveness remains healthy. Record heartbeat and polling intervals.

failureScenarios.procedure: Use deterministic worker-stop checkpoints before commit, after commit and before acknowledgment. Replay the same job reference under a new fence, never terminate an unrelated host process.
Deliver the same synthetic run/batch/intent key twice, including concurrent receipt attempts; compare unique effects and retained attempt records.
Advance a controlled clock past a lease, reclaim the job, then submit an old fence result. The old result must not commit or close the run.
Inject controlled missing/timeout/checksum-mismatch responses around staged-object publication. References cannot become available before verified content.
Inject precommit and acknowledgment-boundary database errors using controlled fixtures, then reconcile the durable receipt before replay.
Use a deterministic in-process provider with scripted quota responses and a controlled clock; assert shared admission across simulated replicas, without any hosted calls.
Freeze a synthetic stage's progress while allowing API and independent queues to respond. Show stage age/failure reason rather than inferring fresh findings from liveness.

churn.protocol: Keep 10000 canonical issues and 3 source variants per applicable issue stable. Each cycle creates one full scan per source with distinct membership; import each scan three times. Renormalize a declared subset with parser-v2 at cycle 16 without inventing a scan. Advance a controlled clock through retention windows, preview expiry, exempt held evidence/active decisions and restore the final consistent snapshot.

retentionPolicies.policy: Move eligible historical payloads to indexed archive manifests; preserve run/variant membership, current projections, notes and active decisions.

Retain age is measured from original source-report ingestion, not reset by archival. Expire only eligible unheld/unreferenced content after a reviewed preview; keep an availability tombstone and provenance links.
Raw bytes may expire independently of compact normalized provenance, but not while held or required by an active decision. Show exactly which original evidence is no longer retrievable.
Archive eligible audit detail with a manifest while preserving decision lineage and required holds. No automatic erasure of active acceptance/suppression approvals.

availabilityPolicy: Archived means retrievable through an authorized archive path; expired means policy-authorized removal. Missing/corrupt means an unexpected integrity or availability failure, never successful retention or remediation.
